title: Fennel: from a won deal to a balanced ledger
tagline: From a won deal to a balanced ledger, with every step posting exactly once.
note: The CRM itself is private and not hosted: the public repo and the showcase site contain only the showcase source. Every screenshot is a real capture of the running app with synthetic data; the in-page tour is a labeled illustration of the app's own rules, not a live backend. Original implementation inspired by ERPNext; no affiliation.
problem:
A small distributor converts won opportunities into sales while keeping stock and the books consistent, without double posting.

Defining workflow: Receive ten units, win an opportunity, convert it to an order without retyping, fulfill three, invoice, take payment: seven units remain, receivables clear and debits equal credits; retrying any step never duplicates a movement or an entry.
built:
One of eleven independent CRM MVPs in a single monorepo, each with its own database, migrations, tests and review packet. This one is inspired by ERPNext and is called Fennel Distribution.

  • CRM, Sales, Inventory and Ledger modules with explicit service boundaries
  • Won opportunity to sales order, fulfillment at moving-average cost, invoice with flat tax, payments
  • Double-entry ledger whose balance and immutability are enforced by the database (deferred balance triggers, reversal instead of deletion)
  • Idempotent commands (Idempotency-Key), locked stock and invoice rows, integrity report, trial balance, customer balances

steps.title: Specify before building
steps.body: An acceptance document names the persona, the bounded scope, what is deferred, and ties every required feature to evidence (a test, an end-to-end journey or a recorded check).

steps.title: Model the database so the rules hold even if the code is wrong
steps.body: A Prisma schema plus a hand-written migration of CHECK constraints, composite foreign keys that pin every record to its workspace, and triggers. The tests try to break these from raw SQL.

steps.title: Build the distinguishing workflow through every layer
steps.body: CRM, Sales, Inventory and Ledger modules with explicit service boundaries

steps.title: Prove it in a fresh clone
steps.body: 20 gate checks pass and 0 fail in a fresh clone of commit 55ab57c54c: 10 unit, 59 integration against a real PostgreSQL, 17 browser tests on the production build, container start, a live black-box check, restart persistence, backup and restore, and a production-dependency audit.

steps.title: Review it as an independent reader would
steps.body: A review packet lists what is implemented, what is measured, what was fixed on the way, and every known limit and release blocker, so nothing here is claimed beyond its evidence.

next:

  • No purchasing, multi-currency, discounts, credit notes or period close; not statutory accounting software
  • All posting transactions of a workspace serialize on the journal counter (fine for a small distributor)
  • Not production-ready: no TLS, proxy or monitoring provisioned
